id: title:fasyy612:keep quill menu item keys unique

review.posthog_relevance: Changes the unique key generation and uniqueness preservation mechanism for menu items in the Quill editor dropdown, potentially affecting how menu entries are identified and rendered.
review.reason: The observed hunk P1.F1.H1 shows a substantive change to the item key construction: the return value is no longer a simple string but a template literal prefixed with the menu index, and an explicit conditional check for custom items is removed. review.uncertainty: The actual downstream impact on menu behavior and whether the removal of the custom-item check could introduce edge cases is not demonstrated by this single hunk; no tests or broader context are supplied. The benefit is inferred rather than verified.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains only one hunk. No other hunks are supplied, so no relationship between multiple hunks or broader change group can be established. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: The itemKey function no longer returns a simple string; it now prefixes the result with the menu index and wraps the key construction in a template literal, while removing the explicit check for custom items.
observations.posthog_connection: This change could affect the unique key assigned to menu items in the Quill dropdown, potentially changing how menu entries are identified or rendered. observations.behavior: A comment is added explaining the rationale for including the index and the shared data-attr behavior, while the previous conditional branch for custom items is removed.
observations.code_quote: // Items in one menu often share a data-attr, so the index keeps keys and radio values unique.
observations.posthog_connection: This comment suggests an intent to preserve uniqueness of menu entries by including the index, which could help avoid collisions when multiple items share the same data-attr. This could relate to menu behavior and could help prevent unintended behavior if shared data-attrs were previously causing key collisions.
